items.prompt: Look at the table. Which plant grew tallest?

head: Plant
Height (cm)
figure.alt: Table of plant heights: bean 12 cm, pea 8 cm, sunflower 15 cm, cress 4 cm.

options.why: The bean grew 12 cm. One plant grew taller.
Cress grew only 4 cm, the least.

hints: Tallest means the biggest height.
Look down the height column.
Find the largest number.
items.explanation: The sunflower grew 15 cm, which is the biggest number in the table.

items.prompt: How many paperclips did magnet C hold?

figure.alt: Bar chart of paperclips held by each magnet: A 6, B 10, C 14, D 4.

hints: Find the bar labelled C.
Look across from the top of the bar to the scale.
The lines on the scale go up in 2s.
items.explanation: The top of bar C lines up with 14 on the scale. Magnet C held 14 paperclips.

items.prompt: How many more paperclips did magnet B hold than magnet D?

figure.alt: Bar chart of paperclips held by each magnet: A 6, B 10, C 14, D 4.

hints: Read the bars for B and D.
How many more means find the difference.
Take the smaller number away from the bigger one.
items.explanation: Magnet B held 10 and magnet D held 4. 10 take away 4 is 6.

items.prompt: Ben tests how far a toy car rolls on different surfaces. What should his two table headings be?

options.why: Ben does not change the colour of the car.
Ben is measuring distance, not the time of day.
The weather is not part of this test.

hints: One column is for the thing Ben changes.
The other column is for what he measures.
What does Ben change, and what does he measure?
items.explanation: The first column shows what Ben changes, the surface. The second shows what he measures, the distance in centimetres.

items.prompt: Children counted minibeasts in the school garden. Which conclusion fits the results?

figure.alt: Bar chart of minibeasts found: under logs 18, on the lawn 6, under stones 14, on the path 2.

options.text: Minibeasts like bright, dry paths best.
options.why: Only 2 minibeasts were found on the path, the fewest.
The numbers were very different, from 2 to 18.

options.text: No minibeasts live on the lawn.
options.why: 6 minibeasts were found on the lawn.

options.text: More minibeasts were found in dark, damp places.

hints: Find the two tallest bars.
Think about what those two places are like.
Are logs and stones dark and damp, or bright and dry?
items.explanation: Most minibeasts were under logs and stones, which are dark and damp. Very few were on the bright, dry path.

items.prompt: Put the steps of an investigation in order.
items: Record the results in a table.
hints: Every investigation starts with something you want to find out.
You predict before you test.
The conclusion comes last, after you look at the results.
items.explanation: First ask a question and predict. Then test and measure, record the results, and finally write a conclusion.

items.prompt: The chart shows how high a ball bounced when dropped from different heights. Which sentence is true?

figure.alt: Bar chart of bounce height for each drop height: 50 cm drop gave 20 cm, 100 cm gave 40 cm, 150 cm gave 60 cm, 200 cm gave 80 cm.

options.text: The higher the drop, the higher the bounce.

options.why: The bounce changed from 20 cm to 80 cm.

options.text: The 50 cm drop gave the highest bounce.
options.why: The 50 cm drop gave the lowest bounce.

options.text: The ball bounced higher than it was dropped.
options.why: Every bounce was lower than its drop height.

hints: Look at how the bars change from left to right.
The drop height grows from left to right.
Do the bars grow too?
items.explanation: Each time the drop height went up, the bounce went up too. The higher the drop, the higher the bounce.

items.prompt: Use the pattern in the chart. Predict the bounce for a drop of 250 cm.

figure.alt: Bar chart of bounce height for each drop height: 50 cm drop gave 20 cm, 100 cm gave 40 cm, 150 cm gave 60 cm, 200 cm gave 80 cm.

hints: Look at how much the bounce grows each time.
Each extra 50 cm of drop adds the same amount of bounce.
The 200 cm drop gave 80 cm. Add one more step.
items.explanation: Each extra 50 cm of drop adds 20 cm of bounce. So 250 cm should give 80 + 20 = 100 cm.

items.prompt: A table heading says Time (s). The s stands for ___.
hints: Time can be measured in different units.
A stopwatch counts these.
There are 60 of them in a minute.
items.explanation: The s stands for seconds. Units go in brackets in table headings.

items.prompt: Which is the best way to show how many children chose each favourite fruit?

options.why: Line graphs show how something changes over time.
A map shows where places are, not how many chose each fruit.

hints: Each fruit is a separate group.
You want to compare amounts.
Which chart is made of blocks you can compare?
items.explanation: A bar chart shows a separate bar for each fruit. You can compare the heights quickly.

items.prompt: Mia measured her plant every week. Which result is probably a mistake?

head: Week
Height (cm)
figure.alt: Table of plant height: week 1 2 cm, week 2 4 cm, week 3 6 cm, week 4 3 cm, week 5 10 cm.

options.why: Week 1 fits the pattern of growing 2 cm a week.
Week 5 fits the pattern: 2 more weeks of 2 cm after week 3.

hints: Look for a pattern in the heights.
A healthy plant does not get shorter.
Check each week against the one before.
items.explanation: The plant grew about 2 cm each week, so week 4 should be about 8 cm. A plant cannot shrink from 6 cm to 3 cm, so 3 cm is probably a mistake.

items.prompt: Draw a bar chart of these results. Label both axes.

head: Surface
Distance (cm)
figure.alt: Table: the toy car rolled 40 cm on carpet, 90 cm on wood and 120 cm on tiles.

criteria.label: Draws each bar to the correct height

hints: Put the surfaces along the bottom.
Choose a scale that counts up in 10s or 20s.
items.explanation: The bar chart should have the surfaces along the bottom and distance in centimetres up the side. The tiles bar is tallest at 120 cm.

items.prompt: Sixteen children chose a favourite fruit. Fill in the missing number.
hints: Add up the numbers you can see.
7 plus 5 plus 4 makes 16.
Take 7 and 5 away from 16.
items.explanation: 7 plus 5 is 12. 16 take away 12 is 4, so 4 children chose apple.
